New Hampshire woman trapped in urgent care clinic — after staff locks up and leaves

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A New Hampshire woman suffering from an asthma attack visited an urgent care only to get locked inside when staff closed shop for the night —  and forgot she was still there.

Tia Chandler was waiting at ConvenientMD in Keene for a steroid shot to combat her asthma on Sept. 24 when clinic workers suddenly vanished.

“I pop my head out and said, ‘Hello? Hello?’ And, then I got a little nervous,” Chandler told WCVB.

“So, I ran to the front, thinking that there was just a skeleton crew on and that they were, you know, cleaning the office,” she recalled.

“And so, I went to the office. ‘Hello?’ And, looked around and there’s nobody there, and I kind of panicked a little and texted my husband, ‘They locked me in. Call 911.’ I’m, like, panicking.”

A desperate Chandler tried opening a door, which triggered the alarm.

She then phoned police for help, calling the entire ordeal bizarre and frightening.

“Very shocking. Just like, I can’t believe this just happened to me, because literally when I was thinking in my head, sitting there at 8:10, ‘They would never lock me in there. That’s crazy talk,” Chandler said.

“That only happens in movies or on a show, not in real life.”

The whole experience put a sour taste in her mouth — and she won’t be returning to the clinic anytime soon.

When asked by WCVB if she would ever go back, Chandler said “probably not.”

“And we’ve utilized them quite a bit in the past.”

ConvenientMD expressed remorse in a statement to the outlet: “We sincerely regret the incident that occurred on Thursday, Sept. 24, at our urgent care clinic in Keene involving one of our valued patients.

“Clearly, this should never have happened. … We have taken steps to ensure this won’t happen again and we remain committed to providing the Keene area with the high-quality care we have been providing for more than a decade,” the statement continued.

[Source 2 — www.abc.net.au] (URL: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-10-15/perth-woman-charged-after-allegedly-poisoning-colleagues-curry/107270322):

Woman charged after allegedly poisoning colleague's curry with snail pellets

The Perth woman is due to face court accused of adding the pellets to the curry in an apparent attempt to poison another woman with whom she was in a "personal relationship".

The woman allegedly contaminated her colleague's curry with poisonous snail pellets. (File photo of curry) (Flickr: Junya Ogura)

A Perth woman has been charged after allegedly putting poisonous snail pellets in a colleague's curry in an apparent attempt to poison her.

Police said the incident happened in February at a workplace in Oldbury, a semi-rural area south-east of Perth.

They said the alleged victim, a 58-year-old woman, brought a container of curry to work to share with colleagues.

During a morning tea break, the curry was shared among employees and eaten without issue.

But at lunchtime, the woman went back to eat more of the curry and noticed bright green granules in the food.

After tasting it, she reported experiencing numbness to her tongue.

The food was kept and was given to police.

Police allege between morning tea and lunch, a 43-year old woman accessed a chemical storage shed, then went back to the staff room where the food was kept and allegedly added snail pellets to the curry.

They have charged her with one count of endangering the life, health or safety of a person.

Police say the two women were also in a "personal relationship" together.

An investigation by detectives allegedly identified the substance as snail pellets containing metaldehyde, a poisonous substance.

She is due to appear in Armadale Magistrates Court on November 5.
